The wide, tall complex at about x≈380 is the odd beat. Its peak reaches roughly twice the height of the neighbouring QRS complexes, and it is broader and more bizarre in shape.

Counting the sharp QRS spikes from the left gives: 141 (1), 208 (2), 274 (3), 341 (4), 380 (5), 472 (6), and so on.

The beat at x≈380 comes only about 40 px after beat 4, while normal R-R intervals are about 65–67 px. It is followed by a longer gap to beat 6 at x≈472, a compensatory pause. This pattern, with an early wide premature beat and a pause, points to a premature ventricular complex.

FINAL ANSWER: 5
